profile.campus: Papillion/Springfield, Sarpy County, Nebraska (Meta's Sarpy data center campus, nine buildings planned across two municipalities)
profile.address: State Highway 50, Springfield, Platford-Springfield I Precinct, Sarpy County, Nebraska, 68059
profile.reading:
This building is one of at least five mapped structures in this registry belonging to Meta's Sarpy Data Center, a hyperscale cloud campus that Facebook's parent company has built in and around Papillion and Springfield, Nebraska, since 2017. The project began under the shell company name Raven Northbrook LLC, and Sarpy County officials initially reviewed it as a proposal called the Sarpy Power Park, with an original plan for four data center halls of about 610,000 square feet each straddling Nebraska Highway 50 and Capehart Road. Facebook's identity behind the project became public in 2017 after a Nebraska certificate of authority filing traced the company back to its Menlo Park headquarters address. Groundbreaking followed in 2017, the plan grew to six buildings and about 2.6 million square feet by 2018, and the first buildings came online in 2019. In 2021 Meta, as the company had by then renamed itself, expanded across Capehart Road into the neighboring town of Springfield, adding roughly a million square feet in a phase reported at the time to carry a roughly 400 million dollar price tag, at which point the whole complex was renamed the Sarpy Data Center. A further expansion announced in July 2022 added a ninth building, after Meta acquired more than 500 acres in Springfield south of the original Papillion site, bringing the announced campus total to nine buildings and about four million square feet. Meta's own materials describe cumulative investment in Nebraska north of two and a half billion dollars, construction that moved more than three million cubic yards of dirt and used more than six thousand tons of steel, and a peak construction workforce reported at different points as roughly 1,300 to 2,000 skilled trades workers. Operational staffing has grown from a reported 150 or so full time employees around 2022 to more than 300 in Meta's most recent public materials, spanning electricians, HVAC specialists, server technicians and engineers. Meta describes its operational Sarpy buildings as LEED Gold certified.

The company's own explanation for choosing Sarpy County centers on power. In 2017 Omaha Public Power District created a new renewable energy rate structure specifically so Facebook could buy essentially all its electricity from renewable sources rather than the half renewable, half conventional blend OPPD had offered previously, and OPPD built roughly 400 megawatts of dedicated wind generation, reported at the time as sited in Holt County, with a further 450 megawatts under board consideration soon after to keep pace with the load. Meta's most recent Nebraska fact sheet instead describes the campus as supporting 320 megawatts of new clean and renewable energy in the state overall, a figure that almost certainly reflects cumulative renewable power purchase arrangements tied to the campus rather than generating equipment installed on any building, and it should not be read as onsite generation in the narrow sense of physical hardware on site. No public source this research turned up reports the campus's actual IT load in megawatts, OPPD's firm utility interconnection capacity in megawatts, or the size of any diesel standby generation fleet, whether for the campus as a whole or for this building specifically, so those three figures remain unknown here. Flat land, an interstate and highway corridor, fiber routes already serving the Omaha area's other data centers, and Nebraska's state and local tax incentive programs, including sales and use tax and personal property tax relief historically available under the Nebraska Advantage Act and its 2020 successor the ImagiNE Nebraska Act, rounded out the location's appeal. Sarpy County is a genuine regional data center hub, home to Google's competing campus among others as well as Meta's, and in 2023 county officials said existing personal property tax incentives across the county's four large data centers were costing roughly 5.8 million dollars a year in forgone county revenue, a figure that describes the county's whole data center base rather than Meta's project alone.

What is not known publicly is extensive. No zoning, permit, or assessor record reviewed for this project ties a specific building number, address, or square footage to this building's OSM footprint at latitude 41.1122, longitude -96.1416. Based on that coordinate alone, this building sits at the southern and eastern edge of the four buildings in this registry researched here, a position more consistent with the Springfield expansion land Meta acquired in 2021 and 2022 than with the original 2017 to 2019 Papillion core to the north and west, but that inference is geographic only and not confirmed by any public document. Nothing in the public record distinguishes this building's individual IT capacity, utility service size, or backup generation from its siblings, and it is entirely possible that no public source ever will, since Meta discloses these figures, when it discloses them at all, at the campus level rather than the building level.

profile.regional_context: Sarpy County, in the Omaha metro area, has become a regional data center hub alongside Meta: Google operates its eighth Sarpy County facility in Papillion, and the area also hosts Fidelity, Yahoo, and other technology employers, per WOWT/Sarpy Chamber reporting. Meta's own 2025 Nebraska fact sheet instead describes the campus as supporting 320 megawatts of new clean and renewable energy in the state. reading.body:
Meta's Sarpy County campus straddles Papillion and Springfield in the Omaha metro area, about nine miles southwest of downtown. Meta began construction in 2017 and has announced plans for nine buildings totaling more than 4 million square feet across the site. The operator does not publish per-building power consumption, exact square footage, or confirmed final building count; only the campus-wide investment figure of more than $2.5 billion is documented. This facility is one of five Meta structures OpenStreetMap has grouped at the Sarpy location and represents the largest visible operator presence in Nebraska's published data center capacity, though no operator in the state has published a megawatt figure.

The campus draws on 100% renewable wind energy and carries Meta's commitments to LEED Gold certification, net-zero operations, and water-positive status by 2030. Meta has funded a 320 megawatt renewable generation project in Nebraska to supply the campus and reports more than $4.1 million in direct funding to local schools and nonprofits. The site's power and renewable-energy anchor suggest the Sarpy location is positioned to host large-scale AI workloads, but without published per-building IT load figures, the actual present or planned compute density on campus remains unknown.

Sarpy County has become a regional data center hub; Google operates an eighth facility nearby in Papillion, and the area also hosts Fidelity, Yahoo, and other technology employers. The concentration of operators reflects Omaha Public Power District's renewable-generation capacity and Nebraska's economic-development incentives for capital investment, though a specific power-purchase agreement naming Meta by facility is not published. Nebraska's lack of any published facility-level megawatt specifications limits visibility into the state's true AI infrastructure footprint.
